correctness.rationale: A choice of split counts t_s yields N_s=a_s+b_s−t_s+t_{s−1}, which is automatically nonnegative for 0≤t_s≤b_s. Divisibility by s is sufficient as well as necessary because within-size labels can be grouped arbitrarily. The predecessor y must have residue t−a_s−b_s modulo s; on that residue the additive transition cost is the sum of a function of t and y/s. Thus each extremum needs only one optimally scored predecessor on that residue, equivalently optimizing m(y)+floor(y/s) or M(y)+floor(y/s). Since the sum of all state-array lengths is n+∑b_s, scanning even the full arrays at each next stage is linear, as are the timestamp operations and retained parent storage. At s=1 the residue is unique, and at s=n the only allowed output state is zero. Parent traversal and batching distinct labels into groups realizes both bounds, including n=1. Explicit output is linear in the size of its label list. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; its finite brute-force comparisons are corroboration, not the general proof.
residual_risks: Word-RAM statement assumes constant-time standard integer arithmetic including quotient/remainder on O(log n)-bit words, not the bit cost model.
